job.title: Treasury Operation Associate
job.description:
Treasury Operation Associate

About Us
Symmetry Investments is a global investment company with offices in Hong Kong, Singapore, London, New York, Jersey, Cayman Islands and Dubai (DIFC). We have been in business since 2014 after successfully spinning off from a major New York-based hedge fund.

At Symmetry Investments, we seek to engage in intelligent risk-taking to create value for our clients, partners and employees. We derive our edge from our capacity to generate Win-Wins – in the broadest sense. Win-Win is our fundamental ethical and strategic principle. By generating Win-Wins, we can create unique solutions that reconcile perspectives that are usually seen as incompatible or opposites, and encompass the best that each side has to offer:
We integrate fixed-income arbitrage with global macro strategies in a novel way.
We invent and develop technology that focuses on the potential of human-machine integration.
We build systems where machines do what they do best, supporting people to do what people do best.
We are creating a collaborative meritocracy: a culture where individual contribution serves both personal and collective goals - and is rewarded accordingly.
We value both ownership thinking AND cooperative team spirit, self-realization AND community.

We are looking to hire an exceptional candidate to work in Symmetry’s growing Treasury Operations function. Among the traits we value are: curiosity, motivation, resourcefulness, good taste, common sense, a commercial orientation, humility, courage, and we would be particularly interested in candidates with some programming knowledge, although this is not a pre-requisite.

We value virtue and capability over experience and credentials, although those are also valuable. We have previously hired candidates with 2-5 years experience in similar functions, but are open to other profiles, especially for those who may be very capable technically.

Treasury Operations at a large RV fund like Symmetry is extremely complex and there are new challenges and idiosyncrasies in cash movements that we face on a regular basis. The need to question the status quo, understand complex arrays of cash movements in a real time basis and make quick judgements on funding requirements is at the heart of this role. There is no back stop behind Treasury Operations. Understanding that responsibility and driving change to improve efficiency, transparency and reduce operational risk is key to ensuring the fund can continue being successful.
Work to be done in the first 3 to 6 months

  • The successful Treasury Operations Associate will spend the first 6 months within the role learning the following 5 areas:


Margin Call Management

  • Main contact on all margin calls for SMF and SAF, which covers ETD, Cleared OTC & PB
  • This includes analysing the margin call data, validating variation margin and substantiating initial margin - through attributing the day on day change in IM from a linear change in risk, or a non-linear change in portfolio margin offsets. Any differences to the Prime Broker will be disputed and investigated
  • Liaise with IFS on all GMRA and ISDA margin calls and investigate / resolve any breaks e.g. Independent Amount disputes, MTM differences, price differences, trade universe differences
  • Aid in onboarding AcadiaSoft Margin Manager collateral workflow system and be the user instructing, receiving, disputing and reconciling ISDA & GMRA margin calls within the system – and identifying / implementing any systematic improvements to support STP margin call management

Trade Capture

  • Instruct all non-cash collateral and treasury investments movements in the market, monitoring the settlement status of the movements and following up on any fails
  • Capture the trades into OT, ensuring the positions reflect the movements as instructed by Front Office
  • Reconcile positions and haircuts, including the alignment of the security against the correct exchange in OT versus the street

Liquidity Monitoring

  • Projection of EOD cash balances prior to UST rolls at midday
  • Monitoring and controlling for known nuances with counterparties (for example, margin vs settlement double counting under Barclays GNA and Citi CPM), and highlighting the cash impact to Front Office
  • Reconciling projection versus actual EOD cash balances, and substantiating any differences
  • Monitor intraday equity at Barclays and Citi, ensuring enough equity is on account to release all outgoing liabilities

Cash Management

  • Monitoring settlement of all incoming wires at our PB cash accounts, escalating pending wires with the counterparty and requesting SWIFT messages to help locate the funds
  • Instructing cash moves across various counterparties, including cash investments instructed by the Front Office, and sweeping coupons from custody accounts

FX Rolls

  • Attribute the cash balances that require rolling forward (using FX Swaps) into where those balances come from (cash IM or VM, haircut, settled cash, unrolled FX balances, coupons) and communicate any unrolled balances to Portfolio Managers for rolling
  • Monitoring of restricted currency balances pertaining to KRW initial margin, MYR/THB coupons
  • Monitoring of intraday cash balances post instruction to TAs to roll, ensuring we do not sit long or short unnecessary cash balances at our PB

Day-to-day responsibilities of the team include:

  • Monitor initial margin requirements, and understand and explain changes
  • Instruct and capture movements of cash and non-cash collateral
  • Internal stakeholder management with Portfolio Managers, Trading Assistants and Risk through monitoring of Portfolio FX exposure, cash balances and initial margin
  • Ensure good value settlement of all cash and non-cash movements
  • Understand the constituents of treasury funding balances
  • Monitor intraday liquidity
  • Produce end of day cash reports
  • Manage dispute resolution process with our administrator on our bilateral trading agreements
  • Overseeing accurate and timely processing of cash wires
  • Process improvement


The role will require a significant amount of stakeholder management, including with:

  • external GMRA & ISDA counterparties
  • Prime Brokers & ETD / OTC clearers
  • vendors like OpenGamma
  • fund administrator IFS
  • internally with TAs, the Treasury Portfolio Manager, other Portfolio Managers, Operations and Legal
  • Clear communication, quick learning and comfortable with analysing data is also key.

What to Expect from our Interview Process
Our interview process is not a cookie cutter process and changes based on the candidate. In general, you should expect:

- An introductory meeting and an aptitude assessment. The aptitude assessment is not a pass/fail test, and we do the same aptitude assessment for all candidates coming to Symmetry - so it cannot be a test of competency for a certain role. We're trying to understand what you're good at and what you're bad at, to try to form a role around your strengths and weaknesses.

- A meeting with a member of the team for an open discussion on your background, experiences and how you may fit into the team.

- A meeting with someone technical. We're not looking for everyone to be a software developer, but we do like having technical people meet candidates to see how they approach complex problems, how they can break them down and solve them, and how they learn.

- Iteration from there, based on the feedback from the interviews and any further interviews to try to figure out where you'd best fit within Symmetry and what role we can create for you.

job.title: Good Junior who wants a Business Manager/Junior COO role
job.description:
CassonX are delighted to be the EXCLUSIVE recruiter for this Global Macro Hedge Fund that is due to launch at the end of Q1 2027, with $500m (at least) committed for 2 years in comingled and SMAs. With focus on Emerging Markets, this exciting business is the brainchild of a super-smart professional with an illustrious successful career in the one of the major banking names. They are a very small company, and where this is very early stages, you must be excited to be early in their tenure as a business. This company offers hybrid working conditions, and looking for someone to grow using the proven COOs knowledge to develop your skills into more of a Business Management type role.

To be considered for this tremendously exciting opportunity, CassonX are looking to identify someone with Operations/Middle Office experience for Futures / ETD and ideally FX knowledge, and willing to oversee their outsourced operations function which is with a major name in the industry. If you have further exposure to OTC, TRSs and Repo products, then this is highly advantageous. You experience will ideally be gained in a Hedge Fund, or form an outsourced type business that focusses on hedge fund or buyside clients, however they would be willing to consider those coming from a Prime Brokerage background to.

Given the budget, it is anticipated that the successful person will offer 1 to 5 years experience in the industry, but it's all about personality with this hire. Yes, you need to be smart and switched on, but this is such a rare opportunity to have such a broad role, we really need someone who not just looking for a typical Operations / Middle Office role, but actually wants to learn and do more.

This incredibly broad role will encourage you to see and support everything that the COO does. It it is more of Junior Business Manager role, where you will expected to learn and grow into, but the main foundation is making sure all Operations is supported and well looked after. However, you will also see things like reviewing the NAV packs, get involved with Audit cycles of the company and the funds as example. Being open on responsibilities is what will make you an exceptional candidate, especially as they want someone to start pre-launch and help shape the business for the future.

CassonX Limited are committed to providing fair employment opportunities to all applicants. We encourage anyone to apply, regardless of their background, and promote a fair and inclusive recruitment process based on merit. If you require any assistance throughout the interview process to improve your experience, kindly let us know.

job.title: COO - Shared Sercices - Broker Dealer / Investment platform, must know custody (NDA)
job.description:
The candidate needs to come from traditional brokerage or an investment platform, and have custody experience. They cannot come from a clearing house, CCP, crypto, prop trading firm, or fund management.

FYI - The question you need to ask is: Has the candidate held direct management responsibility within a regulated broker-dealer, with off-shore delivery teams, that acts as custodian of clients' securities, including maintaining the client asset books and records, reconciling positions with external custodians/CSDs, administering corporate actions, and fulfilling client asset safeguarding obligations?


CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER

Legal entity GTN Group Holding Limited (GTNGH) Reports to Group Chief Executive Officer

Location London/Dubai Scope Group Operations

About GTN
GTN provides global investment infrastructure to banks, brokers, wealth managers and fintech platforms, including execution, clearing, settlement, custody and API-based or co-branded technology solutions. Regulated broker-dealer entities (the “Hubs”) serve institutional clients through B2B and B2B2C models, supported by centralised Group Operations.
Role overview
Reporting to the Group CEO, the COO directs Group Operations staff, budgets and resources, and is the principal service-delivery partner to each GTN regulated Hub. The mandate is to build reliable, scalable and cost-efficient operations that support GTN’s expansion across markets, products, jurisdictions and client segments.
Group Operation functions span Hub’s outsourced post-trade operations, reconciliations, client onboarding due diligence, delegated regulatory reporting processes, revenue capture, intercompany allocations, operational loss monitoring, revenue assurance, operational finance and treasury.
Key responsibilities
1. Post-trade operations and market infrastructure
• Ensure resilient multi-asset class operational capabilities (equities, ETPs, bonds, funds and options, plus where applicable CFDs, FX and Commodities), including fractionalisation and internalisation.
• Deliver trade booking, clearing and settlement instructions, matching, position and cash movements, settlement funding, custody administration, failed-trade resolution, client reporting and related operational support across relevant markets and products.
• Oversee corporate actions end-to-end: event validation, client notification, voluntary elections, dividends, splits, rights, tender offers, entitlement calculation, payments, withholding taxes and claims.
• Execute securities transfers in/out, custody asset servicing, withholding-tax claims, operational client communications and resolution of disputes with counterparties; ensuring workflows meet the service expectations of institutional customers and counterparts.
• Maintain strong service relationships with clearing brokers, custodians, depositories and settlement agents; support Hubs in key counterparty SLA reviews and contract negotiations.
• Deliver operational readiness for new products, Hubs, markets and settlement-cycle changes (including T+1), in coordination with Hubs, Product and Technology.
2. Reconciliations, safeguarding and tax administration
• Ensure daily and periodic reconciliation of trades and settlements versus external broker and counterpart records, with timely correction of breaks.
• Maintain accurate Hub client and house ledgers, and aggregate cash and custody records, independently reconciled against evidenced sub-custodian and bank positions, with timely correction of breaks; maintain break logs, ageing, remediation evidence and appropriate segregation between preparation and review.
• Perform delegated safeguarding controls, including client money reconciliations, internal custody checks, shortfall or prudent segregation processing, records integrity and complete evidence for Hub oversight.
• Oversee operational withholding-tax and transaction-tax processing, including working knowledge of W-8BEN / W-8BEN-E / W-8IMY, treaty rates, Qualified Intermediary obligations, FATCA and Section 871(m) dividend equivalents.
3. Client onboarding and ongoing due diligence
• Execute Hub delegated risk-based CDD/EDD, UBO verification, PEP/sanctions screening, source-of-funds analysis and periodic AML/KYC refresh, using Hub specified criteria and audit trails.
• Lead delivery of end-to-end operational onboarding for Omnibus and fully disclosed Model B clients, as well as execution-only or settlement-only counterparts, from information capture to completed review and Hub approval.
• Assess Model B Institution AML/KYC control evidence, reliance and information-sharing arrangements and periodic assurance testing; supporting Model B underlying-customer due diligence.
• Sponsor digital onboarding with audit trails, automated document extraction, verification, screening and risk scoring; maintain oversight of human review for higher-risk decisions and provide transparent feedback on Customer and Model B Institution reliance arrangements.
4. Surveillance, monitoring and regulatory reporting support
• Coordinate visibility of Hub regulatory-reporting timetables, working with Hub Compliance and Finance on periodic and event-driven returns, including trade/transaction, prudential capital and liquidity, client-money/assets and AML-related reporting.
• Prepare, validate and technically submit delegated BAU reports, manage submission acknowledgements, rejects and corrections, and provide evidence for Hub sign-off, regulatory queries, audits and inspections; direct regulatory engagement and local regulatory capital and prudential calculations remain with the relevant Hub.
• Maintain reporting timeliness, completeness and exception dashboards, with maker-checker control, clear service owners and immediate notification of missed deadlines or material reporting errors.
5. Revenue assurance and direct expense controls
• Ensure complete and accurate capture and collection of brokerage commission, fees and rebates, whether collected through settlement or invoice.
• Maintain effective billing and revenue controls, including invoice generation, receivables monitoring, and reconciliation of revenues against underlying trades, contracts and fee schedules. Identify and recover missed or undercharged revenues.
• Match and reconcile clearing, custody, exchange, settlement and other direct costs to underlying activity; verify counterparty invoices and recover overcharges.
• Provide timely, reconciled revenue, invoice and collections to Hubs and Group Head Office Finance for month-end close and profitability reporting by client, Hub and market.
6. Operational transformation and growth
• Drive a prioritised improvement roadmap for straight-through processing, automated reconciliations, exception management, corporate actions, reporting and digital onboarding.
• Work with Group and Hub stakeholders to deliver new global operational capabilities for new services, including tax-wrapper accounts, margin trading, treasury (FX and interest on client cash) and SLB services.
• Demonstrate scalable, measurable improvements in service capacity, process accuracy, control quality and customer experience, and operating cost reduction.
• Maintain a practical change and delivery improvement roadmap covering data quality, staff skills, workflow and operational resilience, with embedded controls and measurable outcomes.
7. Intercompany agreements and allocation processes
• Maintain transparent calculations and documented methodologies, collaborating with Group Head Office and Hubs on compliant transfer pricing arrangements.
• Administer the operational elements of inter-Hub trading and service agreements, calculating, reconciling and settling approved revenue-sharing and Group Operations cost allocations.
• Run monthly inter-Hub reconciliation, settlement instruction and dispute resolution cycles, with appropriate records of contractual and methodology changes approved by the relevant stakeholders.
8. Operational incidents, trade errors and losses
• Report to affected Hubs and maintain a consolidated global register of trade errors, operational losses and near misses, including prompt identification, quantification, booking support and threshold-based escalation.
• Drive root-cause reviews, recurring-error prevention, agreed write-off workflows and timely remediation; provide monthly trends and loss reporting to Hubs, Group CEO, CFO, CRO and relevant Board and Hub’s ARCC.
• Coordinate financial loss booking and proposed write-offs, ensuring consistent classification, near-miss analysis, accountability for actions and escalation against approved thresholds.
10. MIS and governance
• Deliver consolidated operational MIS across the group. report comparable activity volumes, financial and operational performance, service quality, incidents, trade losses, revenue assurance, costs and material trends.
• Deliver operational MIS to each Hub, providing activity volumes, financial and operational performance, service quality, incidents, trade losses, revenue assurance, costs and material trends.
• Provide each Hub with its own timely, detailed MIS for the services outsourced to
Group Operations: SLA achievement, processing volumes, settlement fails, reconciliation breaks and ageing, client asset controls, operational incidents and remediation.
Leadership, governance and service performance
• Lead the Group Operations organisation (currently more than 100 people), including staffing, recruitment, performance management, training, resource planning and budgets.
• Build a strong performance culture, with staff development, clear accountabilities and an emphasis on accuracy, client experience, efficiency and early escalation.
• Establish consistent service procedures, cut-offs, controls and SLAs, adapted to Hub requirements; oversee service reviews, management information, quality assurance and prompt issue escalation.
• Maintain effective first-line operational controls, maker-checker review, segregation of duties, documented procedures, auditability, resilience and service continuity; partner with Group Risk and Hub’s Internal Audit on assurance and remediation.
• Manage Group Operations vendors and subcontracted service providers within delegated authority; oversee operational performance data, incident reviews, regulatory and internal audits, and risk-based control testing across the service estate.
Experience and competencies
• 15+ years in securities/brokerage operations, including at least five years leading substantial teams across multiple markets or jurisdictions; proven experience with institutional counterparties and clearing, custody and post-trade infrastructure.
• Strong grounding in client assets controls, operational AML/KYC, surveillance, transaction reporting, tax, revenue assurance and intercompany financial processes; familiarity with FCA, DFSA, MAS and other relevant regulatory environments.
• Proven success in operating multi-entity outsourced and offshore service models, leading complex change, automation or AI-enabled workflows and managing cost, productivity, operational risk and client service quality.
• Hands-on knowledge of global regulatory operating environments and institutional standards, including the needs of banks, introducing brokers, custodians, market infrastructures and B2B2C platforms.
• Experience managing multi-country onboarding, custody servicing, client-asset controls, reconciliations and financial reporting programmes, with strong risk, client and cost awareness.

Business Systems and Operations Executive
Global Fund Media | Draft job specification | 22 October 2026
Reporting to: Melissa Hill, Chief Operating Officer
Key relationships: Workflow and Projects Manager; External Tech Projects Supplier;
departmental leads; marketing, editorial and sales teams;
Location and working arrangements: Minimum 3 days a week in the office
Salary and employment terms: To be agreed.
Initial scope: Individual contributor with no direct reports (potentially one)
Role purpose
Provide practical systems, data and implementation support to the COO, helping Global Fund
Media turn operational priorities into reliable everyday processes. The role connects business
users with specialist developers, improves the usefulness of the company’s databases and
supports the delivery of workflow, lead generation and operational projects.
The successful candidate will be comfortable working directly in business systems, making
authorised routine changes, translating business needs into clear specifications and ensuring
that completed work is tested, documented and adopted.
Systems and database operations
• Maintain and improve CRM records, field structures, segmentation, imports, exports,
deduplication and data quality, working within agreed permissions and change procedures.
• Configure routine views, reports, dashboards, forms and straightforward workflows where
trained and authorised; refer complex development and integrations to the specialist
developer.
• Investigate operational data and system issues, establish their business impact and prepare
clear evidence for resolution.
• Maintain a practical record of system configurations, field definitions, data sources and
dependencies so that processes can be understood and supported by others.
Business requirements and developer coordination
• Gather requirements from the COO and users; document the current process, the intended
outcome and the proposed change.
• Prepare specifications for Monreid covering users, fields, data mapping, workflow rules,
permissions, reporting, exceptions and measurable acceptance criteria.
• Coordinate questions, estimates, dependencies and progress with suppliers; escalate
decisions about cost, scope and priorities to the COO.
• Prepare test cases, coordinate user acceptance testing, record defects and check that
delivered functionality meets the agreed specification before release approval.
Process implementation and project support
• Help Esah implement approved workflows and projects by preparing process maps,
configuring supporting systems, resolving data issues and testing handoffs between teams.
• Write concise procedures and user guides, provide practical training and follow up to check
adoption and resolve recurring problems.
• Maintain technical actions, dependencies, risks and decision records within the project
tracking arrangements managed by Esah.
• Identify repetitive manual work and propose proportionate improvements or automation,
with clear benefits and ownership.
Lead generation and campaign operations
• Support approved lead generation projects through target criteria, data research, cleansing,
enrichment, segmentation and campaign list preparation.
• Help maintain reliable capture of lead source, campaign attribution, ownership and followup
status in the CRM.
• Work with marketing, editorial and sales colleagues to connect campaign activity with
usable contact data and agreed follow-up processes.
• Check data quality and respect recorded consent, suppression and access requirements;
escalate unclear data use decisions to the appropriate owner.
COO operational support
• Take ownership of agreed systems and implementation tasks so the COO can focus on
priorities, decisions and accountability.
• Provide short progress updates showing completed work, next steps, blockers and decisions
required.
• Prepare operational reports and investigate inconsistencies between systems and
departmental records.
• Support the rollout of agreed tools and working practices, including structured document
management where assigned.
Responsibilities and decision boundaries
The COO sets priorities, approves material changes and supplier expenditure, resolves crossdepartmental
decisions and remains accountable for operational direction.
Esah coordinates the overall workflow and project plan, including owners, milestones and
follow-up. This role contributes the systems, data, specification and implementation work
needed to deliver that plan. It does not introduce a second project reporting line.
Monreid owns specialist Zoho engineering and complex technical delivery within its agreed
scope. This role defines business requirements, performs authorised routine configuration and
coordinates testing and user adoption.
Departmental owners approve their business requirements and confirm that the completed
process works for their teams. Technology support providers retain responsibility for
infrastructure, devices and specialist security work under their existing arrangements.
Essential experience and capabilities
• Practical experience in business systems, CRM administration, technical operations, data
operations or a comparable implementation support role.
• Strong IT literacy and confidence working with structured databases, CRM records,
spreadsheets, imports, exports and data quality checks.
• Ability to translate an operational problem into a clear written requirement that a specialist
developer can implement and test.
• Experience implementing processes, documenting procedures, testing system changes and
supporting users.
• Strong Excel skills, including lookups, pivot tables and data reconciliation; careful handling of
confidential business and contact data.
• Clear communication, sound judgement and the ability to manage several agreed tasks
while raising conflicting priorities promptly.
• A practical, service-minded approach: comfortable investigating details, following through
and checking that a change works in everyday use.
Desirable experience
• Zoho CRM administration and familiarity with other Zoho applications.
• ActiveCampaign or a comparable marketing automation platform; lead capture,
segmentation and campaign reporting.
• Familiarity with integrations, APIs, low-code automation, SQL or basic scripting. Specialist
software engineering is not a core requirement.
• SharePoint document organisation and permissions; experience in media, events, financial
services or another commercial information business.
Proposed first 90 days
Days 1–30: Understand priority workflows and data sources; agree responsibilities with the COO
and Esah; review the systems backlog; establish a requirements and testing template; deliver
one agreed practical improvement.
Days 31–60: Take ownership of routine systems and data tasks; progress an agreed Zoho change
with Monreid; support a priority lead generation or process implementation project; document
the resulting procedures.
Days 61–90: Demonstrate a completed change from requirement through testing and adoption;
establish repeatable data quality checks and reporting; agree the next improvement backlog
with the COO and Esah.
How success will be assessed
• Agreed tasks delivered on time, with dependencies and blockers raised early.
• Clear specifications and successful user acceptance testing, with limited avoidable rework.
• Improved completeness and accuracy of priority CRM data, measured against an initial
baseline.
• Reliable campaign lists, lead routing and reporting; commercial outcomes remain shared
with the relevant sales and marketing owners.
• Processes used consistently by colleagues, with fewer recurring manual corrections and less
routine intervention required from the COO.
Specific targets will be agreed after the initial systems and workflow review.

job.title: Europe Head of Options & Clearing Operations
job.description:
GTN Europe Head of Options & Clearing Operations
Location: London
Employment Type: Full-time
Reporting to: GTN Europe Head of Operations
Entity: GTN Europe Financial Services Ltd

About GTN Group
GTN Group is a global financial services and technology provider delivering advanced investment infrastructure to retail brokers, banks, wealth managers, and fintech platforms. GTN enables access to global markets, providing trading, settlement, custody, and data services via API-based infrastructure and co-branded trading apps.
Operating multiple regulated broker-dealer entities worldwide, GTN serves institutional clients in B2B and B2B2C models, supporting neobanks, neobrokers, and digital wealth managers with scalable, compliant investment solutions.
Role Overview
The Head of Options & Clearing Operations is a senior GTN Europe role owning the operational framework for European listed options across the GTN Group, US listed options within GTN Europe, CCP clearing and onward client margining.
The role owns the post-trade operating model across clearing, margin, collateral, liquidity, settlement, reconciliations and operational risk.
The role is GTN Europe’s primary operational relationship owner with Eurex, Eurex Clearing, LCH and Cboe Clear across options and cash-equity clearing, including DCM arrangements.
This is not a product, trading-system or regulatory role; those responsibilities sit elsewhere, including regulatory responsibility with GTN Europe Compliance.
Key Responsibilities
Options & Clearing Operational Ownership

  • Own the operating model for European options across the GTN Group, US options within GTN Europe and GTN Europe’s European cash-equity CCP clearing.
  • Establish clear operational ownership, procedures, controls, escalation paths and service standards within GTN Europe and across relevant Group dependencies.

CCP, Clearing & Market Access

  • Own GTN Europe’s post-trade and clearing operating model, including:
  • Eurex-listed equity and index options cleared through Eurex Clearing,
  • US-listed options cleared through US clearing brokers and European cash equities cleared through Eurex Clear / LCH / Cboe Clear.
  • Hold the primary operational relationships with Eurex, Eurex Clearing, LCH, Cboe Clear and relevant US options clearing brokers.
  • Own operational readiness for GTN Europe’s DCM, exchange and clearing-broker arrangements, including:
  • account structures, static data and standing settlement instructions,
  • trade capture, allocation and clearing confirmation processes,
  • exercise, assignment, expiry and equity-settlement processing,
  • position, trade, cash, premium, fee and collateral reconciliations,
  • break investigation, exception management and escalation,
  • default-management and contingency procedures.
  • Ensure clearing arrangements are operationally resilient, scalable and capable of supporting future client-clearing services.

CCP Margin, Collateral & Liquidity Operations

  • Own operational processes for margin, collateral and liquidity arising from GTN Europe’s obligations to CCPs and clearing brokers, including:
  • daily and intraday margin calls from Eurex Clearing, LCH, Cboe Clear and US options clearing brokers,
  • initial margin, variation margin, default-fund and related obligations arising from GTN Europe’s clearing memberships.
  • Own the operational framework for collateral funding and movement, including:
  • cash and eligible collateral movements to CCPs, clearing brokers and settlement banks.
  • Coordinate margin forecasts, funding requirements and intraday liquidity needs with Treasury, Finance, Risk and Operations.
  • Ensure CCP and clearing-broker margin and collateral calls are validated, approved, funded and reconciled within required deadlines.

Client Margining & Collateral Operations

  • Own the end-to-end process for onward margining of GTN Europe’s options clients, including daily and intraday calculation, call issuance, collection, reconciliation and escalation.
  • Operationalise Risk-approved client margin parameters, including initial and variation margin, house add-ons, concentration charges and collateral haircuts, and own the client collateral lifecycle.
  • Monitor margin utilisation, collateral coverage, overdue calls and shortfalls intraday, triggering restrictions, escalation and close-out or liquidation procedures under approved frameworks.
  • Reconcile client margin and collateral to positions, books and records and relevant CCP or clearing-broker obligations; maintain management information and a model scalable to future client-clearing or GCM services.

Operational Risk & Control Framework
Own the first-line operational risk framework for GTN Europe’s options, CCP-clearing and post-trade activity, ensuring risks are identified, controlled, monitored and escalated.
This includes responsibility for an integrated operational control framework covering:

  • Clearing and settlement controls, including:
  • trade capture completeness and clearing-status monitoring;
  • position, cash, premium, fee, collateral and CCP reconciliations;
  • exercise, assignment and expiry controls for options and settlement controls for cash equities;
  • timely investigation and resolution of failed, rejected or unmatched activity.
  • CCP and client margin and collateral controls, including:
  • independent validation of CCP, clearing-broker and client margin calls and material collateral movements;
  • monitoring of margin utilisation, collateral sufficiency and liquidity at CCP and client level, with reconciliation to positions, books and records and relevant clearing obligations;
  • defined approval and escalation thresholds for exceptional calls, overdue client calls and margin shortfalls, including intraday funding deadlines;
  • controls over collateral eligibility, valuation, substitution and return, with contingency procedures for funding, banking or clearing-service disruption.
  • Operational incident and exception management, including:
  • daily monitoring of breaks, aged exceptions and unresolved reconciliation items;
  • root-cause analysis and remediation of recurring operational failures;
  • identification and escalation of material operational, clearing or counterparty risks;
  • event-driven procedures for market disruption, volatility, expiry and clearing stress.

Ensure these controls are:

  • documented in clear procedures and control standards;
  • consistently applied across GTN Europe and relevant Group dependencies;
  • scalable for European options, GTN Europe’s US-options activity and future client clearing;
  • supported by appropriate MI, KRIs, incident reporting and governance.

DCM Governance

  • Maintain detailed operating procedures, RACI matrices, control inventories and escalation frameworks for GTN Europe’s DCM activities.
  • Ensure operational processes support:
  • listed-options and cash-equity clearing across GTN Europe’s CCP relationships,
  • Omnibus and Model B account-level position, cash, margin-call and collateral records,
  • accurate interfaces between front-office, clearing, CCP, settlement and books-and-records systems.
  • Lead readiness and testing for clearing changes and future client-clearing or GCM services, including related client-margining and collateral processes.

Senior Stakeholder Engagement

  • Act as GTN Europe’s senior operational subject-matter authority for European options, GTN Europe US options, and CCP clearing across options and cash equities.
  • Liaise with the GTN Europe Head of Operations, CEO, Risk, Finance, Treasury and Compliance, and with relevant Group teams supporting the European options offering.
  • Hold the primary senior operational relationships with Eurex, Eurex Clearing, LCH, Cboe Clear, relevant settlement banks and US options clearing brokers.
  • Provide senior operational input into clearing strategy, client-margining and collateral arrangements, material incidents, market-infrastructure changes and potential future GCM readiness.

Skills & Experience
Essential

  • Deep operational expertise in listed equity options and central counterparty clearing.
  • Hands-on experience with European listed-options operations, Eurex or comparable infrastructure, and US options clearing.
  • Senior experience in derivatives operations, CCP clearing, post-trade or institutional brokerage within a European investment firm or broker-dealer.
  • Proven track record managing DCM or GCM clearing obligations, CCP and client margin calls, collateral movements, reconciliations and operational incidents.
  • Strong understanding of:
  • options and cash-equity exchange and CCP market structure,
  • CCP margining, onward client margining, collateral and liquidity obligations associated with direct clearing membership,
  • exercise, assignment, expiry, settlement and operational risk flows.
  • Experience designing and operating robust first-line controls for clearing, client margining and derivatives operations.

Desirable

  • Direct operational experience supporting a DCM or GCM relationship with Eurex Clearing, LCH, Cboe Clear or another major CCP.
  • Experience managing exchange, CCP, settlement-bank and US options clearing-broker relationships.
  • Experience designing or operating client-clearing and onward client-margining models.

The Operations group deals with all post-trade processing at Symmetry; trade affirmation, settlements, lifecycle management, reconciliations, P&L calculations, and collateral and treasury management in collaboration with our treasury front office team.

This is not your typical team of people blindly processing and pushing a button on an excel spreadsheet. Our work is highly analytical, engaging and we contribute to the firms’ enterprise value. It requires a deep understanding of product specific nuances and implications on the broader system to build an operational platform that allows the firm to scale the business.

We work in collaboration with our peers on the investment and non-investment side of the business to not only support them and their front-to-back trading activities but help them generate alpha. Is there a new trading agreement or a way to structure the pricing of their trade which will reduce the operational cost throughout the life of that trade? Is where they are clearing their current flow inefficient from a margin perspective? Operations are the subject matter experts on the trade life cycle and this knowledge is invaluable to traders and their bottom-line P&L.

Activities in the first 3-6 months

  • Monitoring of Fixed Income (Bonds and Repo) and Equity trade flow
  • Monitoring affirmation platforms (Omgeo CTM, TRAX) and resolving exceptions to ensure top day matching
  • Resolving trade breaks and following up on fails to ensure timely settlement
  • Daily T+1 reconciliation of trades, positions, cash balances and financing accruals across our prime, FCM and bilateral accounts
  • Trade query management and resolution in conjunction with fund administrator, counterparties, prime brokers and managed account Operations team
  • Work closely with TAs / traders to resolve potential trading issues
  • Work closely with Treasury team to ensure accounts are funded and non USD currency flat and all payments including for collateral management are processed
  • Management and processing of coupons
  • Establishing workflows e.g. for a new counterparty, and following up to ensure correct set up
  • Monitoring of execution platforms and exceptions management
  • Perform other daily checks and controls
  • Facilitating any ad hoc requests arising from the different portfolio teams and individuals
  • Identifying, documenting root causes to persistent issues that occur in our workflow, and provide proposals on ways to tackle at source
  • Cross training and providing support to other product areas where capacity allows

The Ideal Candidate

  • We are looking for an exceptional candidate with domain expertise in the middle office and operations space.
  • You will be familiar with managing high volume of trading and having input in building controls and systems to manage associated operational risks.
  • You will an excellent understanding of the lifecycle of a trade.
  • You will likely be frustrated at a larger institution and want to have the ability to make an impact on a business and have the drive to make change happen.

What to Expect from our Interview Process

Our interview process is not a cookie cutter process and changes based on the candidate. In general, you should expect:

- An introductory meeting and an aptitude assessment. The aptitude assessment is not a pass/fail test, and we do the same aptitude assessment for all candidates coming to Symmetry - so it cannot be a test of competency for a certain role. We're trying to understand what you're good at and what you're bad at, to try to form a role around your strengths and weaknesses. Short of cheating, we generally do not eliminate candidates at the aptitude assessment stage.

- A meeting with a member of the team for an open discussion on your background, experiences and how you may fit into the team.

- A meeting with someone technical. We're not looking for everyone to be a software developer, but we do like having technical people meet candidates to see how they approach complex problems, how they can break them down and solve them, and how they learn.

- Iteration from there, based on the feedback from the interviews and any further interviews to try to figure out where you'd best fit within Symmetry and what role we can create for you.
